summary: India, Day 202. The transmission chain the graph has carried since March — oil → rupee → gilts → RBI — is running at full pressure and the Fed has added a dollar leg. The rupee opened Thursday at ₹96.00, its first 96-handle since late July, within hours of the Fed's hike (DXY >100); the 10-year gilt is at 7.06%, a one-year high, up 10bp in three sessions; and the sell-side has moved as one to an RBI HIKING cycle — HSBC, Nomura and StanChart all see 25bp on 7 Oct and again in December, with Nomura calling headline CPI through 6% in Oct–Nov. The one datapoint that moved the right way — August CPI at 4.82%, below the 4.9% poll and the graph's 5.0% trigger — was ignored because WPI printed 8.3% on fuel and power. Equities are the calm layer: the Nifty made a five-month low of 23,118.60 on Tuesday (oil $107 + US 10Y >5%, the exact mechanism the 14-Sep brief warned would test 23,000) then recovered to ~23,275 on DII buying (+₹3,908 cr Wednesday); financials and autos led the fall. Foreign flows are the blind spot — NSDL shows only the ₹13,138 cr outflow to 11 Sep already briefed. Diplomatically India is Iran's civilian venue (Pezeshkian's conditional talks offer came via India Today) and a victim of the strait (one Indian seafarer still missing from El Gaia). Deployment: every condition set on 14 Sep is further away — Brent $105 not <$90, the Fed hiked rather than held, FPI unknown, CPI's beat overtaken by rates. The stress is in the currency and the bond, not yet the index; the market is still paying to wait.

recent_signals.headline: **INDIA ACTED — AND IT ACTED AGAINST TEHRAN, NOT WASHINGTON.** Two hard actions, both new to the graph. (1) The MEA SUMMONED IRAN'S DEPUTY AMBASSADOR in New Delhi to lodge a strong protest, condemning 'these attacks and acts of violence targeting seafarers and disrupting free and safe navigation through international waterways.' (2) The DGMA issued **Circular No. 36 of 2026 on 15 July**, directing ship owners, ship managers and RPSL companies to AVOID DEPLOYING INDIAN SEAFARERS on any vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz until further orders — a de facto deployment ban branded 'Seafarer-First.' **This is not symbolic: Indians are ~9-10% of the global seafaring workforce and are heavily concentrated in tanker crews, so a blanket Indian-crew withdrawal is a real constraint on global tanker manning through the strait — a CREWING constraint compounding the transit collapse and the insurance-capacity cap.** **The vector question is now answered and the answer is ASYMMETRIC: India formally protested to Tehran and has NOT protested to Washington**, maintaining a studiously neutral public line on the US strikes ('exercise restraint, avoid escalation, ensure uninterrupted energy supply') and condemning strikes on American bases WITHOUT NAMING IRAN. That tilt sits alongside an unsigned trade deal five days from a cliff; the two are not unrelated. CORRECTION: MEA confirms ONE Indian seafarer killed, not two. CONFIRMED (strong independence: Indian, Emirati and Gulf outlets separately).

**INDIA'S HORMUZ EXPOSURE IS NOT CRUDE — IT IS LPG AND LNG. This reframes the graph's core India-energy mechanism.** Per Kpler (via ThePrint, 16 Jul): Russian crude 2.5 mbpd as of 15 Jul (~50% of imports); Gulf supply (Saudi+UAE) ~1.8 mbpd; **Iraqi crude COLLAPSED to negligible from 1 mbpd in January**; Venezuelan 300-400 kbpd. Net: **~70% of India's crude imports now BYPASS the Strait of Hormuz** — 'Russian crude has become its strongest energy-security hedge, particularly since the Strait of Hormuz disruptions' (Kpler's Sumit Ritolia). **The sting is in the tail: LPG and LNG imports remain critically Hormuz-dependent and are running 50% BELOW pre-conflict levels.** That is India's live shortage — Qatari LPG for subsidised domestic cooking-gas cylinders (a direct FISCAL hit) and LNG for industry and FERTILISER FEEDSTOCK. Hard negative on the Iranian-oil question: Iranian crude is offered at $4-5/bbl under Brent but Russian Urals at ~$6/bbl under, so Russian barrels are cheaper AND lower-compliance-risk; Indian refinery intake is fully contracted through August 2026 and the relevant sanctions waiver expires **21 AUGUST**. None of the four preconditions for Indian state refiners to buy Iranian crude are met. **India is not buying Iranian oil in the near term.** REPORTED (Kpler underneath; high confidence on direction, moderate on the exact 70%).

**THE TARIFF DEADLINE QUESTION IS RESOLVED: 24 JULY, not 22 or 23 — and the cliff may run DOWNWARD.** The mechanism is the lapse of a **10% Section 122 balance-of-payments tariff imposed on all trading partners on 24 February 2026 for 150 days** (24 Feb + 150 = 24 July); Section 122 tariffs are statutorily time-limited, which is why the date is hard. Deal still UNSIGNED at T-5, with the Commerce Secretary saying only that 'the framework deal is ready... to be signed at the right time' with NO timeline — **five days of ministerial silence into a cliff is itself the finding.** Reuters frames India as deliberately holding out for better terms rather than negotiating to the calendar. **NON-CONSENSUS FINDING (moderate confidence on mechanics, low on behaviour): the 10% Section 122 layer is a FLOOR ADDED ON TOP. If it lapses without replacement, Indian goods revert toward MFN — reportedly ~16.5% for cotton apparel but 0% for GENERIC PHARMACEUTICALS and 0-2.5% for machinery, materially BETTER for large parts of India's export book. The real exposure sits in the separate reciprocal-tariff track (cut 25%->18% in February), which is what would actually snap back. Do NOT assume a clean lapse is bearish for Indian exporters.** NEGATIVE FINDING: despite the ~50% Russian crude share, **no sourced report places Russian crude explicitly on the BTA negotiating table** — the energy channel appears as a US ask to 'boost US energy exports to India', a positive ask not a punitive one. Watch item: confirmation of the Indian delegation's departure for Washington is the highest-value tell; no travel by Tue 21 Jul = the deal slips past the cliff. CONFIRMED.

Monsoon improving faster than the graph assumed, but fuel policy is frozen and the official loss numbers are badly stale. **SOWING CORRECTION: 531.25 lakh ha as of 10 Jul, ~16% below year-ago — versus -23% as of 25 Jun. The graph's -21% is STALE; the gap is closing ~5-7pp per fortnight on catch-up sowing. Do NOT extrapolate a crop failure.** Still severe: 397 of 741 districts below-normal rainfall as of 13 Jul (326 deficient, 71 large deficiency), IMD estimating July rainfall below 94% of LPA. Worst crop shortfall is OILSEEDS (-3.13 mn ha), directly inflationary through edible oil where India is ~55-60% import-dependent — a rupee-sensitive import bill at 96.3/USD. FUEL: no excise cut, no OMC compensation, no SPR release 17-19 Jul; the standing position remains Puri's 2 Jul line that any cut is '2-3 months away'. **CRITICAL STALENESS: Puri framed that around crude at ~$70. **THE TRADE-DEAL DIRECTION OF TRAVEL REVERSED AT T-3, AND THE BINDING CONSTRAINT HIT THE STREETS TODAY.** The baseline had an Indian delegation travelling to Washington. Instead **USTR Jamieson Greer came to NEW DELHI** to meet Goyal (18 Jul), and **Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal went to GENEVA**, leading India's 8th WTO Trade Policy Review which opened 21 July; India also acceded to the WTO Fisheries Subsidies Agreement on 20 July. **India's senior-most trade bureaucrat was on a different continent doing multilateral business three days before the cliff.** Negotiations at T-6 to T-3 were held on Indian soil with the US principal travelling — not the posture of a party dictating terms into a deadline. **Still UNSIGNED, amid an unusually dense cluster of denials:** Goyal called deadlock reports 'false and misleading' (18 Jul); the **US embassy issued a 'fake news alert'** (18 Jul); Goyal **denied again** on 20 July. When a minister denies the same story twice in 72 hours and the ambassador intervenes between, the base rate favours the story being directionally right and the denials being about tone. **AND THE DOMESTIC VETO IS NOW PHYSICAL: a farmers' Mahapanchayat against the trade deal took place in Delhi on 21 July; Punjab farmers marched on the capital; the SHAMBHU BORDER WAS SEALED and farmer leaders DETAINED.** The Agriculture Minister issued a pre-emptive assurance on 19 July. **The agriculture red line has converted from a negotiating position into a street-level political cost with detentions attached, three days out, with the US negotiator physically in Delhi. Any assessment that India signs by Friday has to explain past this.** Context: Trump imposed **50% tariffs on Canada and 25% on Brazil** in the same window; Greer's 21 July line was 'US tariff policy wildly successful, more coming.' Trade press flags **Section 301 as the successor instrument** to the expiring Section 122 authority — the 10% layer lapsing is not the end state. **FOUR INDIAN SEAFARERS KILLED BY A RUSSIAN MISSILE OFF ODESA — and India summoned the Russian envoy.** On **20 July four Indian seafarers were killed and one critically injured** when a cargo vessel was struck off Odesa, Ukraine; ten died in total. **The MEA attributed it to a Russian missile attack**, called it 'deeply regrettable,' and — per Economic Times and Hindustan Times — **summoned the Russian envoy.** This is the largest confirmed loss of Indian seafarer life in the war period: **four dead in one BLACK SEA incident versus one confirmed dead in the entire Hormuz theatre. India's maritime manpower exposure has been mis-framed as a Gulf problem; it is at least as much a Black Sea problem.** **THE DIPLOMATIC GEOMETRY IS NOW ACUTE:** India protested to **Tehran** over Hormuz on 14 July; it has now summoned **MOSCOW** — the supplier of ~50% of its crude and its strongest energy-security hedge (~70% of Indian crude bypasses Hormuz) — at the precise moment **Washington is threatening 100% tariffs over exactly that relationship.** India has now publicly named two partner states over harm to its nationals and has **still not protested to Washington.** Also new: **NSA Ajit Doval met the Saudi foreign minister on energy security and the regional situation** — direct Indian engagement with a Gulf principal rather than passive price-taking, and a break from the pure oil->rupee->inflation->RBI framing. **⚠️ REJECTED: a News18 headline of '9 Indian seafarers killed' — the confirmed number is FOUR.** DGMA Circular 36 barring Indian crews from Hormuz voyages remains in force, unamended.
